newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan Internet shopping grows 40-fold in 1996/97.
newsitem.headline: Japan Internet shopping grows 40-fold in 1996/97.

text.p: Internet-based shopping in Japan grew 40-fold in the business year ended on March 31, keeping pace with a fast increase in Web traffic, the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications said on Tuesday.

In its 1997 White Paper on Telecommunications, the ministry said Japanese "cybermall" shops on the Internet sold about 28.5 billion yen worth of goods during fiscal 1996/97, up from 700 million yen the previous year.
But the market was still only one-tenth the size of that of the United States, which grew to 268.68 billion yen during the year, up from 41.7 billion yen, the paper said.
Japan, which had been lagging behind the U.S. and European nations in use of the Internet, also saw a sharp gain in the number of Web users in the past year, the report said.

The number of host computers connected to the Internet increased 172.7 percent in the year to January 31, 1997, totalling 730,000 units, the second-largest after 10 million host computers in the United States.
Host computers -- those which have Internet addresses -- usually serve more than 10 individual Internet users.
The paper also said that Japan's domestic production of telecommunications products totalled 92.6 trillion yen in 1995, 10.3 percent of Japan's gross domestic product.
It was the first time the share of telecoms production had exceeded 10 percent of Japan's GDP, the paper said.
